findings.explanation: HOL4's RESULT_def has the single clause RESULT (Result t) = t. Definition takes the primitive-recursion path (Defn.non_wfrec_defn, Prim_rec.new_recursive_definition, new_specification), so this clause is the only saved theorem about RESULT; its value on Clash is left open. Lean adds the clause RESULT (Clash _) = ARB, so it proves RESULT (Clash x) = ARB and RESULT (Clash x) = RESULT (Clash y) for all x, y, and also RESULT (Clash x) = CLASH (Result y). None of these follow in HOL4: a function returning t on Clash t also satisfies RESULT_def. OUTL, specified the same way, is correctly given by epsilon in Prelude/Basic.lean.
findings.repair:
noncomputable def RESULT {α : Type u} [Nonempty α] : result α → α :=
  Classical.epsilon (fun f : result α → α => ∀ t, f (Result t) = t)
findings.lean_check:
import CandleLean.HolSyntaxLib

example {α : Type} [Nonempty α] (x : α) : RESULT (Clash x) = ARB := rfl

example {α : Type} [Nonempty α] (x y : α) : RESULT (Clash x) = RESULT (Clash y) := rfl
findings.hol4_check: ?f:bool result -> bool. (!t. f (Result t) = t) /\ f (Clash T) <> f (Clash F)

findings.explanation: HOL4's CLASH_def has the single clause CLASH (Clash t) = t, introduced by new_recursive_definition/new_specification; no saved theorem says anything about CLASH (Result _). Lean adds the clause CLASH (Result _) = ARB, so it proves CLASH (Result x) = ARB and CLASH (Result x) = CLASH (Result y) for all x, y. HOL4 leaves these open: a function returning t on Result t also satisfies CLASH_def.
findings.repair:
noncomputable def CLASH {α : Type u} [Nonempty α] : result α → α :=
  Classical.epsilon (fun f : result α → α => ∀ t, f (Clash t) = t)
findings.lean_check:
import CandleLean.HolSyntaxLib

example {α : Type} [Nonempty α] (x : α) : CLASH (Result x) = ARB := rfl

example {α : Type} [Nonempty α] (x y : α) : CLASH (Result x) = CLASH (Result y) := rfl
findings.hol4_check: ?f:bool result -> bool. (!t. f (Clash t) = t) /\ f (Result T) <> f (Result F)
